newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand money market says RBNZ firing blanks.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand money market says RBNZ firing blanks.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous trading day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 91.87 (PREV 91.97) 90-DAYS 8.33 (PREV 8.26)
OVERNIGHT CASH 8.00 PCT (PREV 8.10) US 5-YR 6.05 (PREV 6.10)
RBNZ MCI NZ/MCI 722.87 (PREV 709.64) Reuters NZ MCI-103 vs-115
Yields rose on the New Zealand money market on Monday but reaction to a mid-session Reserve Bank comment that conditions were too loose was muted, dealers said.
"Their gun power was a bit wet," quipped a senior bond dealer.
"The market didn't take fright. There were some keen buyers on the selling," said another dealer.
Yields closed around eight basis points higher in the short end and six points in the long end as the curve inverted slightly more.
Dealers said most of the reaction to the comments of the RB's chief manager of financial markets David Archer came via the currency but even that was low key.
The Trade-Weighted Index closed at at 64.20 from its 64.13 opening.
The RB was prompted to make its comments after the Monetary Conditions Index fell to over 125 basis points below the bank's stated desired level of 825 for the September quarter.
Dealers said there were credibility issues involved.
"Overall, monetary conditions have become too loose, given our current monetary policy stance," Archer said in a statement.

"Consistent with the approach the bank set out in June, we have been allowing monetary conditions increasing room to move as the quarter has progressed, and as our last complete look at inflation pressures becomes more distant.
"We have also been waiting to see whether the drift in conditions in recent days would reverse.
"It hasn't, leaving overall conditions beyond levels that we are comfortable with.
"As usual, the bank remains ready to act if necessary," Archer concluded.
Dealers said to act effectively, the bank would probably have to cut the daily cash target to radically move the market.
"That would make the market sit up straight," a dealer said.
One said markets would carefully monitor foreign investor reaction tonight particularly in the currency. Some may see the higher dollar as a good selling opportunity.
"So if we come in tomorrow and see the MCI at -125 that will be interesting."
